BiblicalUsage: Mena' is the Aramaic word to count and to appoint, and it runs through Daniel and Ezra as the word for putting the right man in the right place. Daniel 2:24 says Arioch was the man whom the king had ordained to destroy the wise men of Babylon, and Daniel 2:49 has Daniel set Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego over the affairs of the province. Daniel 3:12 shows the same appointments turned into an accusation, and Ezra 7:25 has Artaxerxes tell Ezra to set magistrates and judges over the people beyond the river.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe appointing is God's work done through kings and priests: Daniel appoints faithful men, and Ezra appoints judges, and the same word covers both. My position is that who is appointed matters as much as what is decreed, because a faithful appointee can save a province.
